# Textbooks

- Cailin O'Connor, [Modeling Scientific Communities](https://www.cambridge.org/core/elements/abs/modelling-scientific-communities/1ED3515216067E40A37A72094EE3CB15) (if you are off-campus you can access this via [the library](https://search.lib.umich.edu/catalog/record/99187887203306381))

# Readings

\(L\) means that you may need to go through library to access; (S) means that these are suggested readings not required.

- Eric Pacuit, [Voting Methods](https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/voting-methods/)
- Michael Morreau, [Arrow's Theorem](https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/win2022/entries/arrows-theorem/)
- Amartya Sen, [The Impossibility of a Paretian Liberal](https://www.jstor.org/stable/1829633?seq=1) (L)
- Amartya Sen, [Liberty and Social Choice](https://www.jstor.org/stable/2026284?seq=1) (LS)
- David Christensen, [Epistemology of Disagreement: The Good News](https://philpapers.org/go.pl?id=CHREOD&proxyId=&u=https%3A%2F%2Fphilpapers.org%2Farchive%2FCHREOD.pdf) (S)
- Adam Elga, [Reflection and Disagreement](https://philsci-archive.pitt.edu/2940/1/refdis.pdf) (S)
- Thomas Kelly, [The Epistemic Significance of Disagreement](https://philpapers.org/go.pl?id=KELTES-3&proxyId=&u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.princeton.edu%2F~tkelly%2Fesod.pdf) (S)
- Roger White, [Epistemic Permissiveness](https://philpapers.org/go.pl?id=WHIEP&proxyId=&u=http%3A%2F%2Fweb.mit.edu%2Frog%2Fwww%2Fpapers%2FEP.pdf) (S)
- Miriam Schoenfield, [Permission to Believe: Why Permissivism Is True and What It Tells Us About Irrelevant Influences on Belief](https://philpapers.org/go.pl?id=SCHPTB&proxyId=&u=https%3A%2F%2Fphilpapers.org%2Farchive%2FSCHPTB.pdf) (S)
- John Hawthorne, Lara Buchak, and Jeffrey Sanford Russell, [Groupthink](https://philpapers.org/go.pl?id=RUSG&proxyId=&u=https%3A%2F%2Fphilpapers.org%2Farchive%2FRUSG.pdf) (S)
- Jan-Willem Romeijn, [An Interpretation of Weights in Linear Opinion Pooling](https://philpapers.org/go.pl?id=ROMAIO&proxyId=&u=https%3A%2F%2Fdx.doi.org%2F10.1017%2Fepi.2020.45) (LS)
- Jean Baccelli & Rush T. Stewart, [Support for Geometric Pooling](https://philpapers.org/go.pl?id=BACSFG&proxyId=&u=https%3A%2F%2Fphilpapers.org%2Farchive%2FBACSFG.pdf) (S)
- James Joyce, [A Nonpragmatic Vindication of Probabilism](https://philpapers.org/go.pl?id=JOYANV-2&proxyId=&u=http%3A%2F%2Ffitelson.org%2Ftopics%2Fjoyce_1998.pdf) (S)
- Rush T. Stewart & Ignacio Ojea Quintana, [Learning and Pooling, Pooling and Learning](https://philpapers.org/go.pl?id=STELAP-15&proxyId=&u=https%3A%2F%2Fdx.doi.org%2F10.1007%2Fs10670-017-9894-2) (LS)
- Judith Mehta, Chris Starmer, and Robert Sugden, [The Nature of Salience: An Experimental Investigation of Pure Coordination Games](https://www.jstor.org/stable/2118074) (L)
- Robert Sugden, [A Theory of Focal Points](https://www.jstor.org/stable/2235016) (LS)
- Vi Hart and Nicky Case, [Parable of the Polygons](https://ncase.me/polygons/)
- Thomas Schelling, [Dynamic Models of Segregation](https://www.stat.berkeley.edu/~aldous/157/Papers/Schelling_Seg_Models.pdf) (S)
- Robert Axelrod and William D. Hamilton, [The Evolution of Cooperation](https://websites.umich.edu/~axe/research/Axelrod%20and%20Hamilton%20EC%201981.pdf)
- Robert Axelrod, [Effective Choice in the Prisoner's Dilemma](https://esp.mit.edu/download/2dd80247-be60-4e73-b49d-91b5b6988ff0/S12850_axelrod_1980.pdf) (S)
- Alexander J. Stewart and Joshua B. Plotkin, [Extortion and cooperation in the Prisoner’s Dilemma](https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.1208087109)
- William H. Press and Freeman J. Dyson, [Iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma contains strategies that dominate any evolutionary opponent](https://www.pnas.org/doi/abs/10.1073/pnas.1206569109) (S)
- George Akerlof, [The Market for Lemons](https://www.jstor.org/stable/1879431)
- Michael Spence, [Signaling in Retrospect and the Informational Structure of Markets](https://www.nobelprize.org/uploads/2018/06/spence-lecture.pdf)
- Michael Spence, [Job Market Signaling](https://www.jstor.org/stable/1882010) (S)
- Kevin J. S. Zollman, [The Communication Structure of Epistemic Communities](https://doi.org/10.1086/525605) (L)
- Sarita Rosenstock, Justin Bruner, and Cailin O’Connor, [In Epistemic Networks, Is Less Really More?](https://cailinoconnor.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/In_Epistemic_Networks_Is_Less_Really_Mor-FINAL-VERSION.pdf) (S)
- Remco Heesen, [Academic Superstars: Competent or Lucky?](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11229-016-1146-5) (L)
- Robert K. Merton, [The Matthew Effect in Science](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.159.3810.56) (L)
- Hannah Rubin, [Structural causes of citation gaps](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11098-021-01765-3) (LS)
- Michael Weisberg and Ryan Muldoon, [Epistemic Landscapes and the Division of Cognitive Labor](https://www.jstor.org/stable/10.1086/644786?seq=1) (L)
- Johanna Thoma, [The Epistemic Division of Labor Revisited](https://eprints.lse.ac.uk/88129/1/Thoma_Division%20of%20Labour_Accepted.pdf)

## Instructions for Slides

The slides are built using [revealjs](https://revealjs.com). To move around them, the four key things to know are:

1. Left and right arrows move between sections.
2. Up and down arrows move between slides within a section.
3. If you move the cursor to the top left corner a three-bar menu appears. Click on it and you can move between any slides.
4. Or simply use space bar to advance one slide forward at any time.
